subject: portuguese
summary: Most Portuguese cards are tidy: the written-production rubrics are clean band lists, the reading cards attach the right text with no stray questions, and card 9's scheme grouped by morning, afternoon and night is the best layout in this batch. The real faults are in gap-fill listening questions, where the blanks are either long underscore runs that overflow the phone screen (card 3) or have vanished entirely so the sentence is unreadable (card 12: 'Com a na , a idosa começou a nos e impediu-os de o .'). Card 1's scheme contains visible corrupted characters. The long commentary cards give one sample paragraph as a single tick box with no marking criteria for 30 or 40 marks. As in Polish, a language-rule boilerplate note is pasted into the first answer box of nearly every card, and the writing questions have their bullet points run into one line.

issues.title: Gap-fill sentences broken: blanks missing or overflowing
issues.detail: Card 12: the blanks were stripped, leaving 'Com a na , a idosa começou a nos e impediu-os de o .', which cannot be read as a task; the scheme then lists six bare words (mala, mão, bater, assaltantes, continuar, assalto) with nothing tying each to its gap. Card 3: the three blanks are very long underscore runs; on the phone they break the sentence into fragments (', mas', 'e por isso') and the lines run off the right edge of the card, and on desktop one line runs past the column divider.
issues.suggested_fix: Render gaps as short numbered blanks ('Com a (1)____ na (2)____, a idosa começou a (3)____ nos (4)____ ...') and number the scheme answers to match, or show the completed sentence with the filled words in bold.

issues.title: Corrupted characters in the scheme
issues.detail: Card 1's sample answer shows three boxed control-character glyphs in the middle of a sentence ('...das misérias do dia-a-dia, mas 2[?] [?] [?] cada vez era mais difícil...'), an extraction fault from the scheme PDF. It also has a missing space before '(Oh, what a pleasure' and an unclosed bracket. Card 6 has a missing full stop ('em Portugal O choro surge').
issues.suggested_fix: Re-key these scheme passages from the official PDF and add a check that rejects control characters in card text.

issues.title: Long commentary cards: one paragraph, one tick box, no criteria
issues.detail: Cards 1, 6 and 10 (30 or 40 marks) show a single sample paragraph inside one checkbox under 'Tick each part you completed', with no marks, no criteria and no breakdown. A student cannot tell what earns marks. Card 4 is similar and additionally says 'This question cannot be scored here' with a 'Parte I: 30m in all' badge, which is honest but leaves the card with nothing to assess against.
issues.suggested_fix: Present the paragraph as a labelled 'Sample commentary from the scheme' (not a checkbox), split into its two or three ideas as bullets, and show the content/language criteria the scheme applies to this section if it publishes any.

issues.title: Language-rule boilerplate inside the first answer box
issues.detail: 'The examination prints this question in Portuguese and it is answered in PORTUGUESE. The scheme awards half marks for an answer given in the wrong language.' appears inside the first scheme point on almost every card, often above the answer and with odd prefixes ('For "PARTE II":', 'For "Proposta 2":', 'For "Manhã":'). Card 3 repeats the whole completed sentence as a note under each of its three answers. Card 7 adds 'The scheme prices this answer "3 marks: 3 × 1 mark"'.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the language rule once per card as a footnote. On card 3 show the completed sentence once above the three answers. On card 7 say '1 mark each: 5 people; 3 adults; 2 children'.

issues.title: Question text slips: flattened bullets, joined words, stray labels
issues.detail: Cards 2 and 8 run the bullet points into the sentence ('Inclua os seguintes detalhes: • Descrição das personagens; • Descrição do espaço; • O que acontece.'). Card 10 has 'centradono' (missing space) and 'Proposta 2' stuck on the front of the essay title. Card 11 flattens three answer labels into 'When is the event? Date: From: To:'. Card 5 fuses the general instruction and the term into one line and keeps a trailing semicolon ('...expressões. Apartado ao meio (§ 6);'). Card 6 gives the quoted sentence without quotation marks, so instruction and quotation run together.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep bullets as a real list, put quotations in quote styling, show answer labels as separate lines, and fix the typo on card 10.

issues.title: Attachments: sibling options shown; one essay card has no context
issues.detail: Card 2's attached page shows options (a), (b) podcast and (c) new business together although the card is option (a); card 8's page is cropped to option (c) only, which is better. Card 10 has no attachment, so the student cannot see the full proposal as printed. The attachment reader footer truncates its note mid-sentence ('...The scheme awards half marks for an a...').
issues.suggested_fix: Crop writing-task attachments to the option the card covers, or drop them when the task is fully typed on the card.

issues.title: Listening audio did not load in the capture
issues.detail: All four listening cards show '0:00 / 0:00 — The embedded recording could not be loaded'. Possibly a capture-environment problem; worth checking live.
issues.suggested_fix: Verify playback in the live app.

Clean rubric with clear bands and score buttons, and an attachment cropped to just this option.
Four short answers each labelled with the field it fills (Date, From, To).
